title: serving-runtime daily scratchpad 2026-03-22
content:
Morning triage - 2026-03-22

- Quick hits:
  - Prod p99 spike last night on model-rank-11 (eu-west). Root cause likely batching latency regress after 3.2.0 kernel swap. See RINF-2418.
  - Small memory leak observed in kv-cache eviction path on CUDA 13.2 driver nodes.
  - Canary rollout for quantized-4bit-v2 paused due to mismatch in tokenization results on long prompt (>4096).

Bugs to prioritize:
- RINF-2418: p99 latency regression after kernel swap. Repro locally with microbench (seq_len=2048, batch=8) -> p99 80ms -> 170ms. Suspect radix-sort fallback in attention kernel. TODO: run with PERF_LOG_LEVEL=3 and capture kernel launch times. (assign Miguel)
- RINF-2421: kv-cache leak on long-running streams. Repro: stream 10k tokens continuous, memory rises ~3%/k tokens on G5s. Hypothesis: stale ref in cache_shard when resizing. Add address sanitizer on CPU side and instrument GPU allocations with NVTX. (assign Ava)
- RINF-2422: tokenization mismatch for quantized-4bit-v2 on long inputs. Likely inference-time truncation or different BOS handling in quantized converter. Quick patch: canonicalize tokenizer config at load-time; add unit test. (assign Priya)

Perf TODOs / experiments:
- Re-run kernel matrix-mul benchmark with CUTLASS 3.5 on staging (tags: kernel-bench-3.5). Compare to 3.2 results. Capture SM occupancy and achieved TFLOPS.
- Try alternative attention layout: pack QKV interleaved vs separate. Microbench seq_len distribution: 128 (60%), 512 (25%), 2048 (15%) — optimize for tail.
- Batching policy tweak: lower max_batch_delay from 5ms -> 3ms for model-rank-11 to reduce p99, measure throughput loss. A/B via rollout route config.
- KV-cache compaction: implement periodic compaction that consolidates small shards every N requests. Measure CPU overhead.

Kernel notes (brain dump):
- attention.cu: consider early-exit when key padding all zeros (sparse prefix). Add branch to skip softmax reduction if all -inf.
- radix-sort fallback causing 2x latency in some dims; prefer shared-memory bitonic for <2048 keys. Check memory footprint trade-offs.
- use __ldg for read-only weights in beam search kernel to improve L2 hit.
- NVTX ranges: wrap top-level request scheduling + batching + kernel launches to correlate with tracing.

Repro commands / quick checks:
- repro latency microbench: ./tools/bench --model rank-11 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --iters 100 --trace perf_log.json
- mem leak local: python stress_stream.py --model rank-11 --tokens 10000 --cuda 0 --mem-trace
- kernel timings: export PERF_LOG_LEVEL=3 && ./serving --run-local --bench-config=attention_debug.json

Meeting notes:
- 10:30 sync with infra: discuss CUDA 13.2 rollout schedule. Hold off until we confirm kv-cache leak root cause.
- 14:00 triage: decide whether to rollback kernel 3.2 -> 3.1 for prod if p99 not improving after batching tweak. Ops preference: rollback if >2x p99 for >1h.

Next actions (today):
- [ ] Run microbench with PERF_LOG_LEVEL=3 (Ava, 2h)
- [ ] Add NVTX spans around batching path (Miguel, 1d)
- [ ] Add unit test for tokenizer config canonicalization (Priya, 3h)
- [ ] Draft rollback playbook for kernel swaps and postmortem checklist (Ava + Miguel, 4h)

Notes to self / reminders:
- Save perf traces to S3 under s3://redwood-perf/traces/2026-03-22/model-rank-11/
- Remember to ping infra about driver config; they recently changed G5 kernel flags.
- Follow up on PR #842 for batching policy changes — need docs update in console for new route settings.

Open questions:
- Is the radix-sort fallback triggered by particular key lengths or by an internal heuristic? Need to instrument decision branch.
- Does quantized converter pad tokens differently for >4096 inputs? Check converter v2 changelog.

Quick links / refs:
- RINF-2418 (JIRA): p99 regression
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Confluence: SR-kernel-optimizations (notes + kernel trade-offs)

End of scratchpad.
